claims.claim: Eustathius of Antioch was Patriarch of Antioch from 324 to 330.
Eustathius was a native of Side in Pamphylia.
Eustathius was bishop of Beroea before becoming patriarch of Antioch.
The work De Melchisedech is also known as Epistula ad Alexandrum Alexandrinum.
The work was addressed to Alexander of Alexandria.
The work deals with the interpretation of Hebrews 7:3 concerning Melchizedek.
Eustathius was a prominent opponent of Arianism at the Council of Nicaea in 325.
Eustathius was deposed and exiled due to intrigues of pro-Arian bishops, particularly Eusebius of Caesarea.
A fragment attributed to ninth-century Patriarch Photius of Constantinople was shown to be an excerpt from Eustathius's De Melchisedech.
The fragment's misattribution to Photius was discovered through examination of its relation to the Photian commentary and its manuscript provenance.
